newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate down as cash demand eases.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate down as cash demand eases.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates were down 245 basis points at 21.80 percent in early dealings Monday.
Traders said market speculation that had pushed rates up on Friday faded as players had managed to cover short liquidity positions.
"Rates soared on Friday, as many banks were overdrawn on accounts pending with the central bank. Secondary rates ahd to subside today as most have almost squared positions now," a trader said.
Analysts said the money market in recent days saw a tug-of-war between players who were short on paper and those who were short on liqudity.
Banks have until Wednesday to settle balances outstanding on checking accounts they hold with the central bank.
Now that liquidity pressures eased, they said, the market could resume its customary focus on the peso-dollar rate and U.S. long bond yields.
Overnight rates on bank paper mirrored government rates, falling 210 basis points to 22.40 percent.
Liquidity of 1.244 billion pesos was due to return to the system from prior central bank operations.
